cohort: The study included singleton, cephalic pregnancies at >=37 weeks' gestation with term prelabor rupture of membranes (PROM) and an unfavorable cervix (Simplified Bishop score (SBS) <=5), excluding those with spontaneous labor onset or cesarean delivery without induction.
finding: In women with PROM and an unfavorable cervix, DVI use did not increase adverse outcomes and was associated with significantly reduced oxytocin use compared to intravenous oxytocin administration.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery rates were comparable between the DVI group (78.3%) and the oxytocin group (73.3%), with no statistically significant difference (p = 0.52).
